plan.name: Postpartum Return to Movement — 2-Week Introductory Block
plan.description: A gentle 2-week starter block for a client 4 weeks post uncomplicated C-section, cleared for light activity only. Focuses on diaphragmatic breathing, pelvic floor reconnection, posture, and progressive walking. No abdominal loading, no heavy lifting, no high-impact. Designed for home use with a yoga mat only.

goals.name: Pelvic Floor Reconnection
goals.description: Re-establish neuromuscular connection with the pelvic floor and deep core via breathing and gentle activation drills.

goals.name: Build Walking Tolerance
goals.description: Gradually increase daily walking duration from 10 to 20 minutes by end of week 2.

phases.name: Foundation — Breathe & Reconnect
phases.description: Weeks 1–2. Establish diaphragmatic breathing, gentle pelvic floor activation, posture awareness, and short walks. No abdominal exercises, no lifting. All floor work is supine or side-lying to avoid incision stress.

activities.name: Glute Bridge Isometric Hold (low range, no abdominal strain)

exercises.name: Modified Child's Pose (avoid pressure on incision — use wide knees)

days.name: Day 4 — Breathing, Pelvic Floor & Hip Mobility

activities.name: Supine Hip Abduction (clam shell prep — side-lying)

days.name: Day 1 — Breathing, Pelvic Floor & Glute Activation

activities.name: Glute Bridge (full range, controlled — stop if incision discomfort)

days.name: Day 4 — Posture, Hip Mobility & Pelvic Floor

activities.name: Wall Posture Stand (head, shoulders, hips touching wall — gentle thoracic awareness)

exercises.name: Gentle Cat-Cow (minimal lumbar flexion — avoid pulling on incision)

activities.name: Self-Assessment & Trainer Check-In: note any incision discomfort, pelvic floor symptoms (leaking, heaviness, pressure), energy levels, and readiness for 6-week OB clearance appointment.

checkpoints.name: End of Week 2 — Pre-6-Week OB Check

measurements.note: Pelvic floor symptoms: any leaking, heaviness, or pressure during or after exercise?
Incision comfort during movement — any pulling, pain, or numbness?
Energy and sleep quality this week.

questions: Are you experiencing any pelvic floor symptoms (leaking, urgency, heaviness)?
Any pain or pulling at the incision site during exercises or walking?
Do you feel ready to progress after your 6-week OB clearance?

notifications.message: STOP and rest if you experience: pain at the incision site, pelvic heaviness or pressure, leaking urine or stool, dizziness, or unusual bleeding. Contact your OB if symptoms persist.
Reminder: your 6-week postnatal OB check is approaching. Clearance at that appointment is required before progressing to Phase 2 of this programme.
